units.translation: I ask the gods for release from these toils, a device for the year-long watch, where μῆκος [length] is in M, which Stanley and Valckenaer corrected, on Herodotus 4, 151. The words φρουρᾶς ἐτείας μῆχος [a device for the year-long watch] are a paraphrase of the preceding τῶνδ᾽ ἀπαλλαγὴν πόνων [release from these toils], which, placed without such an explanation, could not be understood by the spectators. The codex, with a point placed after ἐτείας [year-long], has μήκος δ᾽ ᾿ ἣν κοιμώμενος [and length, which he was sleeping], where an interpolator of the scholia (in the right margin) wrote, τῶν κατὰ τὸ μῆκος τῆς ἐτείας φρουρᾶς [of the things according to the length of the year-long watch], and, what is even more absurd, (in the left) ἦν ἐπὶ μῆκος κοιμώμενος [he was sleeping at length]. μῆκος [length] written for μῆχος [device] as μυκὸν for μυχόν [recess] in Eumen. v. 160. For thus the codex has it there, not μυχόν, as has been falsely stated.
staining his father's hands with streams of virgin-slaughter.
It is not fitting to stain a day of good omen with a tongue of evil tidings.
staining bright water with evil inflows and mud.
of hostile kinsmen and those staining the race, where Hermann conjectures ἐχθρῶς ὅμαιμον καταμιαινόντων γένος [hostilely staining the kindred race].

whom could any house hold, staining upon its roof? where μιαίνοντα [staining] cannot be understood, about which different scholars have conjectured different things, of which one conjecture worthy of mention is Weil's ἔχων – ἰαίνοιτο [holding – may he be warmed], by which the hiatus between ἔχοι [may hold] and ἐπί [upon] is also removed.
Ch. 859 μιανθεῖσαι πειραi κοπάνων [stained by the edges of the cleavers].
to be called cowardly rather than murderous.
There is no old age of this pollution.
holding unenviable pollutions of this victory.
you stained the inner chamber with pollution.
the mother-killing pollution is washed away.
for he had assaults of two pollutions. Thus Elmsley for μίασμάτων [of pollutions].
the earth stained with pollutions of blood.
you have spoken a pollution not to be outshot.
saying that a double pollution appeared before the city.
a woman, a pollution of the land and of the native gods.
a mother – a father-killing pollution and an abomination of the gods.

he will beget another avenger in his head from that one.
μίγνυμαι [I mix myself] to have intercourse
and he mixed the dear milk with a clot of blood.
and in the earth the creatures are mixed with blood-flow.
and the black one will be mixed (or ἀμμεμίξεται [will be mixed together]), where av from av was made in M, so that ἀμμεμίξεται might seem to be written.
Is there not some story that Zeus had intercourse with a mortal?
for a god desiring to have intercourse with this mortal woman.
for it is laden with white and dark and ruddy mulberries.
